name: Familial Partial Lipodystrophy, Köbberling Type

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical diagnostic criteria for Familial Partial Lipodystrophy, Köbberling type

criteria.description: Selective loss of subcutaneous adipose tissue predominantly affecting the limbs and trunk with relative preservation or accumulation in the face and neck
Presence of insulin resistance, diabetes mellitus, or dyslipidemia associated with lipodystrophy
Positive family history consistent with autosomal dominant inheritance pattern
Lack of mutations in genes commonly associated with other FPLD types (e.g., PLIN1, PPARG)
Normal or mildly elevated serum creatine kinase levels

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of partial lipodystrophy distribution with metabolic complications and compatible family history
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic testing may be inconclusive; diagnosis is primarily clinical.

laboratory: Elevated fasting glucose and insulin levels indicating insulin resistance
imaging: MRI or CT showing selective loss of subcutaneous fat in limbs and trunk
other: Clinical examination revealing characteristic fat distribution pattern
Family history consistent with autosomal dominant inheritance

distinguishingFeatures: More generalized fat loss including face and neck
Earlier onset and more severe metabolic complications
Near total loss of adipose tissue
More severe insulin resistance and metabolic derangements
Usually presents in infancy or early childhood

redFlags: Rapid onset of severe insulin resistance in young patient
Severe hypertriglyceridemia with risk of pancreatitis
Family history of similar fat distribution and metabolic complications
references: Orphanet: Familial partial lipodystrophy, Köbberling type - ORPHA:79084
